CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Wards
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
A ward is one ring of the settlement. A market town has three: the old town behind the high wall, the suburb behind a lighter one, and the open countryside around them.
Everything else hangs off a ward. Its wall, its towers, its gatehouses, and the districts that decide what gets built inside it.
The order in the list is the order from the middle outwards. The innermost ward is the one the generator protects best and fills first, so put what matters there.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Districts
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
A district is a building programme. It says what the generator should put into this ward and how much of it.
Each line is either a category (Workshop, HouseSmall) or one specific piece (Workshop_Baker). Min and max bound how many of them are built. Weight decides how often a piece is drawn when several fit the same category.
A piece listed under a category counts towards that category's limit. That is why the Baker sits indented under Workshop instead of standing next to it.
Crop plots and animal pens belong to a district too. That is how the generator knows a farmstead gets fields and a tavern does not.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Walls
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
The wall pieces this ward is built from. The generator picks from the list whenever it needs a stretch of wall, so several entries give a wall that varies along its length.
Depth is how thick the ring is. One is a palisade, three is a town wall with a rampart walk on top.
Where a mountain meets the line, the mountain is the wall and nothing is built in front of it.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Field emplacements
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
Towers and other defensive works that sit in the wall ring.
The generator spaces them along the wall by itself, at the corners first and then along the long straight runs. How many fit follows from the length of the wall, not from a number you set here.
The size of the largest tower in this list also sets how much room the planner reserves at every corner, so a very large tower makes the whole outline coarser.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Gatehouses
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
Where a road crosses the wall, a gatehouse is built.
The number follows from the roads, not from a setting. The planner lays out the approach roads first and puts a gate wherever one has to pass through the ring, then checks that every gate can actually be reached from outside.
A piece used here needs a passable opening. Without one the ward is sealed and the whole layout is discarded.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Anchors
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
An anchor is a marked area inside a piece where something happens once the piece is placed.
Connect anchors tie the piece to its surroundings. Wall is where the town wall docks, Outside tells which side faces out, Anbau is where annexes attach.
Loot anchors place objects from an object list and fill them from a loot table. Object anchors place objects from an object list with a chance, without loot. Pawn anchors bring in people or animals from a pawn list, with a role that decides whether they stay and fight or run.
An anchor whose list does not exist marks the piece red in the editor.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Farmland
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
Crop plots and animal pens for the open countryside.
A crop plot is grown around a rural building, not dropped on the map at random. Which buildings get one is decided by the district the plot is listed under. Min and max bound how many plots that building may have.
A pen holds one kind of animal, drawn from a unit list. The herd size is the second row, indented under the pen.
Both get a fence with one gate. Where rock or water already closes the line, no fence is built in front of it.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Settlement plans per faction
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
Which of your settlement plans are used when the player walks into a base of this faction.
The assignment is not stored on the faction. It is stored as factionTags inside the plan, and the generator collects every plan whose tags match the faction. Two mods can therefore both serve the same faction without either one overwriting the other.
A plan that names no faction at all serves every faction. That is why a fresh plan shows up everywhere until you assign it.
Removing works only for plans attached by faction name. A plan attached through the faction category has to be detached in the plan itself.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Takeover
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
Nothing you assign here shows up until RimWorld actually hands faction bases to this generator. That is what the takeover switch does.
It writes one patch file into the Patches folder of the current mod. The patch swaps a single generation step, Settlement for CBF_Settlement, and leaves everything else in place, so faction bases keep their rocks and their power lines.
If a patch file is already there, the operation is added to it and the rest of the file is kept. Switching the takeover off removes only that operation, not the file, unless nothing else is left in it.
A faction with no matching plan falls back to RimWorld's own settlement, never to an empty map.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Annexes
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
An annex is a small piece that attaches to a house: a stable, a woodshed, a beer garden. Everything about it is data in the categories and pieces, nothing is fixed in code.
Annex categories on the house's category say which annexes may attach to it. An empty list takes the list of the parent category.
Chance per anchor is the chance that an annex is built at one annex anchor of the house, default 0.6. At most caps the number of annexes per house, default 2.
Repeatable belongs on the category of the annex itself. Yes allows the same annex several times on one house.
Weight decides which annex is picked when several fit. For annexes, a weight below 1 is also the chance that this annex is tried at all.
The anchor is a Connect anchor named Anbau. On the house it lies on the outer wall. On the annex it lies either on its outer wall, when both share that wall, or one cell outside its shape, when the annex only touches the house.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: At the wall
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
How much a piece wants to stand against the town wall. The planner reads it when it places buildings.
Forbidden keeps the piece away from the wall. Avoid, Allowed, Preferred and Strongly preferred weigh the spots along the wall lower or higher. Required forces contact: the piece is only placed where it touches the wall.
A piece without a value of its own takes the wall contact of its category. Yes there means Preferred.

CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.label: Ward gate
CustomBaseFramework.HilfeDef.description:
The thing that closes the passages through this ward's wall, for example a wooden gate for a palisade and an iron gate for the town wall.
Empty uses the gate of the palette, which is what most wards want.
